transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… I’ve been hearing things at work. Voices, I guess. From the call-light speaker, sometimes the hallway vents. They’re telling me patient records have been changed. It sounds clear, like someone is standing right there, but the unit is quiet and no one else seems to hear it.
Can you tell me more about what the voices are saying and how it relates to your work with patient records?

They… they’ll say certain charts aren’t right. Like a record was changed, or something was switched. It comes through the call-light speaker, sometimes the vents in the hall. It sounds real clear, like someone’s right beside me, but when I look around, it’s quiet and nobody else reacts.
Are the voices you're hearing telling you to do something or are they more critical of what's going on with the patient records?

They’re mostly saying which records were changed. Not really… telling me to do anything, just pointing it out, like, “that chart’s been altered.” It comes through the speaker or the vents, clear as someone right next to me.
Do the voices ever tell you to take any specific action regarding the patient records they mention?
No… not really specific actions. They just say which records were changed, like they’re pointing it out through the speaker or the vents. It sounds right there, but nobody else seems to hear it.
Do you feel like you have to respond or react in some way when the voices point out the altered patient records?

I… I feel like I should pay attention, at least. When it comes from the call-light speaker or the vents that clearly, like somebody’s right next to me saying a record was changed, it’s hard not to react… even if nobody else hears it.
How do you feel when you hear these voices pointing out the altered patient records?

Uneasy. Like… on edge, I guess. It sounds so clear, like it’s coming right out of the call-light speaker or the vents, somebody standing there saying which chart was changed. And when nobody else hears it, that makes me feel… I don’t know. Worried.
Do you ever find it hard to keep track of what the voices are saying or to make sense of their messages?

Not usually. It’s… pretty clear when it happens. Like it’s coming from the call-light speaker or the hallway vents, saying which records were changed. I don’t really have to piece it together. It just… says it.
Have the voices affected your ability to work or interact with your colleagues?

Yeah… it has. I was taken off the floor during a shift because my supervisor said my handoffs and charting weren’t safe anymore.

I don’t really like talking about it. My husband’s been handling things at home I normally do, too. It feels like… my reputation at work, and LPN school, all of that is kind of falling apart.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable?

Yeah… sometimes. There are days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I’m supposed to fix things at work. But if my husband, or one of the nurses, tells me to slow down, I get really irritated. I snap at them… like they’re getting in the way of something important.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or energetic that lasted for several days or longer?

Yes… for a few days sometimes. I’ll feel like I’m finally awake, like I’m supposed to fix everything at work. But then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get… really irritated. Like they’re blocking something important.
When you feel like you're finally awake and supposed to fix things at work, do you find yourself being more productive or taking on more tasks than usual?

Yeah… I guess I do. I’ll finish a full shift and still feel like I have all this energy, so I come home and start cleaning or rewriting notes, sorting things… pacing around the kitchen.

My husband will be asking me to just sit down, and I… don’t really want to.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or energetic that lasted for a week or longer?
Yeah… longer than a week. It’s been… about two months now, since they asked me to help lead that wound-care documentation rollout.
When you're feeling really awake and energetic, do you find you need less sleep than usual?
I’m… not really sure. I mean, my sleep’s been off, but I don’t know if I’d say I need less. I just don’t always notice it.
Do you believe the voices you're hearing are actually telling you the truth about the patient records being changed?

I… yes. I think they’re telling the truth.

The wound-care charts don’t look right. There’s a pattern there, and management doesn’t want it seen. My supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but… I can tell they’re watching what I write now. Because I’m the one who caught it.
Do you think the voices you're hearing could be mistaken about the patient records being changed?

No… I don’t think so.

I know what I’m seeing in those wound-care charts. It’s a pattern, not just late entries or coding errors. My supervisor can say that, but… I can tell they’re watching what I write now, because I’m the one who noticed it.
Do you think it's possible that the changes in the patient records you're seeing are just mistakes or misinterpretations, rather than an actual conspiracy?

No… I don’t think it’s just mistakes.

I know what I saw in the wound-care charts. There’s a pattern there, and management doesn’t want it seen. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding errors, but… I can tell they’re watching what I write now. I’m the one who caught it.
If someone could prove to you that the patient records were not actually changed, would you be able to accept that?

I don’t know… if it was real proof, maybe I’d have to look at it.

But right now I know what I saw in those wound-care charts. It’s not just coding mistakes. There’s a pattern, and… they don’t want it noticed. I can tell they’re watching what I write because I caught it.
Do you think the voices and the pattern you see in the wound-care charts are connected to each other?

Yes… I think they’re connected.

The voices come through the call-light speaker sometimes, or the hallway vents. They’ll say which records were changed. It’s clear… like someone right next to me, even when the unit is quiet. And nobody else seems to hear it.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally sad or depressed that lasted for several days or longer?
I’m… not really sure. I mean, I’ve had bad days, but I don’t know if I’d call it that for several days. I don’t really keep track.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or energetic that lasted for two weeks or longer?

Two weeks… I don’t know if I’d say it like that.

Some days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I’m supposed to fix what’s happening at work. But then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get angry… like they’re getting in the way of something important.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent psychotic symptoms, including hearing voices that provide a clear and coherent message, which is a hallmark of schizophrenia spectrum disorders. The voices are not merely a mood-congruent feature, and the patient's delusional thinking about the patient records being changed and a conspiracy supports this diagnosis. While the patient exhibits some mood symptoms, they do not meet the full criteria for a manic or hypomanic episode, and the psychotic symptoms are not solely explainable by a mood disorder.
